mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or 20-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in 3 months signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or 60-day forward returns in periods of rising unemployment are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real GDP (GDPC1) signals a weakening demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are revised downwards.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns during GDP declines are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or 5-day forward returns in periods of rising industrial production are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or 20-day forward returns in periods of strong payroll growth are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% in 3 months, it signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the broader economy feels the effects.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or 60-day forward returns in periods of declining housing starts are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals an inflationary environment with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary period with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or 20-day forward returns in high inflation and high-rate periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) increases by more than 1% in a quarter and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% in the same period, it signals a strong demand environment with a robust labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and consumer spending rise.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 1% and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or 60-day forward returns in periods of strong GDP growth and falling unemployment are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
